account: Heelan's write-up followed on 22 May 2025. Heelan is an independent vulnerability researcher auditing ksmbd (the Linux kernel's in-kernel SMB3 server). He used a known bug (CVE-2025–37778) to benchmark OpenAI's o3 via the plain application programming interface (API), with no scaffolding, agents or tools. Given about 12,000 lines covering all SMB command handlers, o3 reported a previously unknown use-after-free in the handler for the SMB “logoff” command. sess->user can be freed while another connection bound to the same session still uses it. The Linux kernel CNA's record describes the fix (“ksmbd: fix use-after-free in session logoff”) with commits in five stable branches. Linuxiac reports the upstream response was fast and patches were merged for every maintained branch. Heelan calls it, to his knowledge, the first public case of a large language model (LLM) finding a vulnerability of that nature.

ai_role.statement: The model produced the finding unprompted during a benchmark. Heelan selected the code, validated the report and handled disclosure. He notes the model also produced false positives in other runs. The account is the independent deployer's own, corroborated by the CVE record and third-party coverage, not by OpenAI.

claim_basis: Sources: one independent news report, a registry entry and the deployer's report. The cited evidence includes no independent study or report and no finding by a regulator or court.

comparator.after: o3 finds the kerberos authentication vulnerability in the benchmark in 8 of the 100 runs
comparator.against: Claude Sonnet 3.7 and Claude Sonnet 3.5 on the same 100-run benchmark (the known ksmbd Kerberos bug)
comparator.before: Claude Sonnet 3.7 finds it 3 out of 100 runs and Claude Sonnet 3.5 does not find it in 100 runs
comparator.quote: o3 finds the kerberos authentication vulnerability in the benchmark in 8 of the 100 runs. In another 66 of the runs o3 concludes there is no bug present in the code (false negatives), and the remaining 28 reports are false positives. For comparison, Claude Sonnet 3.7 finds it 3 out of 100 runs and Claude Sonnet 3.5 does not find it in 100 runs.

fields.account: Heelan's write-up followed on 22 May 2025. Heelan is an independent vulnerability researcher auditing ksmbd (the Linux kernel's in-kernel SMB3 server). He used a known bug (CVE-2025–37778) to benchmark OpenAI's o3 via the plain application programming interface (API), with no scaffolding, agents or tools. Given about 12,000 lines covering all SMB command handlers, o3 reported a previously unknown use-after-free in the handler for the SMB “logoff” command. sess->user can be freed while another connection bound to the same session still uses it. The Linux kernel CNA's record describes the fix (“ksmbd: fix use-after-free in session logoff”) with commits in five stable branches. Linuxiac reports the upstream response was fast and patches were merged for every maintained branch. Heelan calls it, to his knowledge, the first public case of a large language model (LLM) finding a vulnerability of that nature.
